key_insight: Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO) aims to teach visual agents to read image evidence rather than rely on plausible guesses. It trains on contrast sets that pair the same question with multiple versions of an image.
problem_solved: When answering questions about ultra-high-resolution photos, agents may guess from common sense instead of zooming in to inspect relevant details. Rewarding only the final answer cannot distinguish a lucky guess from evidence-based reasoning.
method: Train visual agents using CrossRPO, a reinforcement learning approach built around contrast sets.
Ask the same question across several versions of an image to encourage sensitivity to visual evidence.
Support evidence-seeking behavior in agents that zoom into relevant image regions; the supplied abstract is truncated before full training details.
impact: This approach could make high-resolution visual agents more reliable by encouraging answers grounded in inspected evidence. The provided excerpt does not include quantitative results.
